summary: One entry per version of each unit of the chart package (standard simai.linkage 1.0.0, journal-per-version). Renames and removals of a public name are change-journal records (simai.change-lifecycle), kept in the free journal's form in docs/chart/journal.json.

entries.summary: The chart core: data read from records or columns with a field mapping (a missing value is a gap), linear and calendar scales with round ticks, Intl number and date formats, line, step and monotone paths with gaps, min-max decimation past two points per pixel column, band scales, stacks (stacked and normalized, positive and negative apart, gaps kept), pie and donut slices, series facts for the summary, and the keyboard cursor. Not yet released, so the M1 additions stay in 0.1.0.

sf-chart-line, the first chart of the package: one or more series over time, a number or categories; axes, grid, a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table (toggle, visible, hidden), loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-sparkline: one series as a word-sized line, area or bars without axes, with a mark on the last value or the extremes; an image named by its label and a sentence of the data; loading and empty states.

sf-chart-bar: values by category as columns or horizontal bars, side by side, stacked or normalized to shares, sorted on request, with values at the bar ends; a value axis from zero, a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-pie: the parts of one whole as slices of a circle or a ring with the total in the middle, the smallest folded into «Другое» past max-parts; shares inside the slices, a legend with shares that hides parts (beside or under the plot by a container query), a tooltip, a keyboard cursor said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-metric: one number with its label in a number, currency or unit format; the change against a previous period with its meaning (better) said by tone, arrow and word; a limit as a meter with sf-progress-bar's look; the page's status with a hint; a chart slot for an sf-chart-sparkline; the whole tile as one link or button; loading and empty states.
bandPath: the band between an upper and a lower edge, per run, sharing their gaps; a stacked layer's smooth top is the same curve as the bottom of the layer on it.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: bandPath is new, and areaPath and linePath draw as before.

entries.summary: stack: none, stacked (the series as layers, positive up and negative down from zero) or normalized (shares of the whole at each x on a 0–100 % axis, the cursor and the tooltip saying the share and the value); a layer always fills its band, keeps its gaps and shares its kept points with the other layers; the summary says the series are stacked.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: stack defaults to none, so a chart without it draws as before; set stack to stack the series.

entries.summary: settled: the value a costly view shows for data that may change fast; a change after a quiet spell shows at once, a stream at most once per wait, the latest last.

The data table is rebuilt only when the data changes, never on a pointer or cursor move, and at most once per second while data streams; the first data shows at once. A line chart with table="hidden" updating 1,200 points went from 31 ms to 5 ms per update.

sf-chart-parts: the parts of one whole as one thin bar split into shares, with the free remainder of a capacity (max) named «Свободно»; the smallest folded into «Другое» past max-parts; the whole beside the label, a list of the parts with values and shares (or one inline line for a tile), a tooltip, a keyboard cursor said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

lines: series named in lines are drawn as lines with points over the bars (a plan over the facts), never stacked; line-axis own puts them on a scale of their own with its ticks on the far side (a margin over a revenue), always so over a normalized stack; line-format formats their values in the ticks, the tooltip, the live line and the table; the summary says which series are lines; the cursor walks onto a line and select carries it. Vertical bars only.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: lines defaults to empty, so a chart without it draws as before; name series in lines to draw them as lines.

entries.summary: colors: a page's own colour per series, by its key, a Framework role (which follows the theme) or a CSS colour; a value that is not a colour is dropped and one under 3:1 against the background is reported in the console; a series without one keeps the palette by its place, and forced colours are unchanged.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: colors defaults to empty, so a chart draws as before; give it {key: colour} to colour a series of your own.

entries.consumer: Nothing to do: color defaults to empty, so a sparkline draws as before.

entries.summary: palette: the seriess' colours as a named set (vivid, soft, warm, cool, brand), each colour a light-dark pair on the Framework's tone ladder, 3:1 against surfaces 0-2 in both themes and, for the first five, told apart under the three common colour-vision deficiencies; colors still wins for the seriess it names.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: palette defaults to theme, so a chart draws as before; set palette to use a named set.

entries.summary: sf-chart-heatmap: a measure over two categories as a grid of cells (x, y and value fields), coloured by the steps of a sequential scale (one role family) or a diverging one (two families around a neutral middle, which way is better set by better) on the theme's own tones in light and dark; the value written in each cell where it fits at 4.5:1, gaps as outlined empty cells, a legend of the scale, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor over the grid said in a live region, a summary sentence, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.
The diverging scale's middle step is the Framework's --sf-chart-midpoint (pair ui-de2b4437234a) instead of the package's own neutral-90 / neutral-25; in the dark theme it is neutral-20.

sf-chart-funnel: the stages of a process, each a subset of the last (stage and value fields, in the data's order), as bars on a common baseline or centred, the value and the conversion (of the previous stage or of the first) beside each stage, one colour for the measure, gaps as outlined empty tracks, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor over the stages said in a live region, a summary sentence (the overall conversion, the largest loss), the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-gauge: one measured value on a fixed scale (value, min, max) as a half circle or a bar, with bands in their Framework roles' colours and names, a target mark with the distance to it, the value written in its middle in its band's colour with the band's name under it, a meter with a value text for screen readers, a summary sentence, the same data as a table (hidden by default), loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-scatter: one point per row at two measures (x and y fields), with an optional third as a bubble's area (the bubble field), series by colour and mark shape (the series field), a point's name (the point field), a least-squares trend line on request, a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor that walks the points in reading order and goes up and down to the nearest point, a summary sentence with each series' relation in words and r, the same data as a table, the marks on a canvas past 2,000, loading, empty and error states.

bin: a histogram of one measure (auto, about Sturges' count on a round width, or a given width): one touching bar per interval, the count of its rows or the sum of a weight (y), by series and stacked, the axis marked at the intervals' edges, the summary with each series' median and fullest interval.
entries.consumer: Nothing to do: bin defaults to none, so a chart draws as before; set bin to draw a histogram.

entries.summary: sf-chart-box: a box plot of one measure per group (the x and y fields): the median, the quartiles (linear between the two nearest), Tukey's or full-range whiskers (whiskers) and the outliers, worked out from raw rows or given per group (stats), the mean on request (mean), series side by side in a group (series), a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor over groups and series, a summary sentence with each series' highest and lowest median and widest box, the same statistics as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-radar: a spoke per measure (the x field, the first straight up, then clockwise), each series a ring through its values (y fields or the series field) on one scale from min to max, the scale's rings as polygons or circles (grid), a light fill (fill), marks of their own shape per series, a gap that breaks the ring, a legend that hides series, a tooltip with every series on a spoke, a keyboard cursor round the spokes and across the series, a summary sentence with each series' strongest and weakest spoke and the first two compared, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-candlestick: the open, high, low and close of each period (x, open, high, low and close fields) on a price axis, the periods side by side in time order with the axis marked at calendar periods, a rising body hollow and a falling one filled in the success and error tones (colors {up, down}), candles or bars (shape), neighbours merged as a longer period past one per 3 px, a key of rise and fall, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor over the candles, a summary sentence with the change, the extremes and the count of rises and falls, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

sf-chart-waterfall: how a start value becomes an end value through steps (x and y fields), a change floating from the running total to the new one and a total row (the total field) standing on zero, a closing total added (end), thin lines joining the bars, each bar's value written with its sign (value-labels), the success, error and neutral tones (colors {up, down, total}), a key, a tooltip with the change and the total, a keyboard cursor over the steps, a summary sentence with the start, the end, the steps that added and took away most, the same data as a table, loading, empty and error states.

entries.consumer: Nothing to do: a page's format words read as before; a page may now write decimal-<n> with two digits.
entries.summary: chart-core/format.js formats numbers and dates through the core's SF.format (core.runtime 1.20.0, pair ui-c3015f76bcc2), which took its number words from this file; the chart keeps only its axis-tick and full-date forms and its argument order. decimal-<n> now reads up to 20 digits, as the core does; nothing else a chart says changes.
